title: Generic types and cmp.Ordered
hints: cmp.Ordered is the standard constraint for types that support < and >: integers, floats and strings. Pair[K, V] is a generic struct; you build one with Pair[K, V]{Key: k, Value: v}.

For Entries, collect the map's keys, sort them with slices.Sort (which needs cmp.Ordered), then build the pairs in that order. GroupBy appends each x to the slice at key(x), which keeps the original order inside each group.

Entries: keys := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m)); for _, k := range keys { out = append(out, Pair[K, V]{k, m[k]}) }. GroupBy: g := map[K][]T{}; for _, x := range xs { k := key(x); g[k] = append(g[k], x) }.
